site_article.dek: Freepik's AI suite has a new name. Here is how its image and video generators work, what the free plan gives you and when you need to pay.

paragraphs.text: Freepik's AI tools now live under a new name. The company relaunched as Magnific on April 28, 2026, and freepik.com now sends you to magnific.com. Your login, plan and existing licenses did not change, according to the company. If you want to know how to use Freepik AI, it is the same suite: an image generator, a video generator, an upscaler and editing tools in one place, alongside a stock library of more than 250 million assets.

The selling point is not a model of its own. Magnific mostly gives you other companies' models, such as Google's Nano Banana and Veo, Kling, Seedream, Flux and OpenAI's GPT Image and Sora, behind one prompt box and one credit balance. This guide covers the image generator, the video generator, what the free plan really gives you, and what you may do with the results.
How to use the Freepik (Magnific) AI image generator

paragraphs.title: 1. Sign in and open the AI Suite
paragraphs.text: Create an account or click Sign in, then open the AI Suite from the top menu. The Image Generator is one of the tools listed there.

paragraphs.title: 2. Write a prompt
paragraphs.text: Type what you want to see in the prompt field. The optional AI prompt feature can rewrite a short idea into a more detailed prompt. If you have a picture but no words, Upload image to describe writes a prompt from the image for you.

paragraphs.title: 3. Choose a style, aspect ratio and model
paragraphs.text: Pick a style and an aspect ratio, then a model. The help center says there are more than 30 models, including Nano Banana, Seedream, Flux, GPT Image 2, Ideogram, Recraft and Mystic. If you do not want to choose, set the model to Auto. You can make 1 to 4 images per prompt.

Use Auto for your first tries. Once you like a result, note which model made it and pick that model directly. Quality varies noticeably between models, so the same prompt can look very different from one to the next.

paragraphs.title: 4. Add references when you need control
paragraphs.text: Under References, click + Add to attach a Character, an Object, a Style, a Color palette, a Camera setting or an Effect. You can combine them. To start from your own picture instead, click Upload in the prompt field, then Use image.

paragraphs.title: 5. Click Generate and find your results
paragraphs.text: Click Generate. Finished images appear under Recent creations and stay in the History tab, so you can come back to them later and keep editing on the same page.

If you need the same person in many images, Magnific lets you train a custom character from photos and call it with a short tag such as @jane. Training takes 10 to 30 minutes, per the help center. Only use photos of people who have agreed to it.

paragraphs.title: Prompt 1: A clean product shot
paragraphs.text: A [product] on a plain [color] background, soft studio light from the left, shot from slightly above, sharp focus, lots of empty space on the right for text

paragraphs.title: Prompt 2: A social media header
paragraphs.text: Wide banner image for a [topic] blog: [main subject] in the center, calm colors, simple shapes, no text, plenty of space at the top
How to use the Freepik (Magnific) AI video generator

paragraphs.title: 1. Open the Video Generator
paragraphs.text: Go to the AI Video Generator from the AI Suite homepage. It makes video from text, from an image, or from a first and a last frame.

paragraphs.title: 2. Write the prompt and pick a model
paragraphs.text: Type a prompt, then choose the model, aspect ratio and duration. The list includes Veo 3.1, Kling, Hailuo, PixVerse, Runway, Seedance, Wan, Sora 2 and LTX-2, and resolution depends on the model. Enhance prompt with AI and the Prompt Editor are optional helpers.

paragraphs.title: 3. Animate an image, or set the ending
paragraphs.text: To animate a picture, use the Image tab. Turn on End image when you want to decide what the last frame looks like. Multi-shot lets you build up to 6 shots, and some models can add sound effects.

paragraphs.title: 4. Click Generate video
paragraphs.text: Click Generate video. Clips are typically 4 to 15 seconds long, so plan longer pieces as several shots and join them in an editor.

paragraphs.title: Prompt 3: Bring a photo to life
paragraphs.text: Slow push in toward [subject]. Light wind moves [hair, leaves, fabric]. Camera stays steady, natural light, no sudden cuts.
Freepik AI free plan, credits and prices

The free plan gives you up to 20 AI images per day using the in-house model, according to the help center. It has no credit balance, and you cannot buy extra credits on it. The documentation does not list a free allowance for video.

Paid plans run on credits, and each tool costs a different number of credits. The pricing page lists Premium at $20 a month, Plus at $45 and Pro at $110 when billed monthly, with lower prices for annual billing. Plus and higher plans include Relax mode, which the company says gives free generations on most image models, while most video models and the upscaler still use credits. The help center notes that credit costs can change.
Using Freepik AI images commercially

Commercial use needs a paid plan. The help center says AI-generated images and videos may be used commercially, that paid plans include a commercial license, and that free plans are limited to personal use with attribution. It also warns that the company cannot guarantee copyright ownership of AI output in every country, and that you are responsible for making sure your results do not copy someone else's work or show real people without their consent.
What Freepik AI is bad at

An independent review from Vmake found that image quality varies a lot between models, that complex prompts often need several attempts, that credits get expensive for heavy users and that the strongest models sit on higher tiers. The Next Web noted that Magnific uses the same frontier models as its rivals, so its edge is the workflow rather than the models.

If you only ever use one model, the company that makes it may sell it to you more cheaply on its own site. Magnific makes most sense when you switch between many image and video models in one project.
